harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 4.2.7 cluster (Alpine 3.23), created the `payments` vhost with a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all three nodes, and created an application account `app_user` (no admin tags) with full configure/write/read permissions scoped to `payments`. Demonstrated that durable messages survive the loss of any one node: stopped node2's rabbitmq-server, confirmed quorum (node1+node3) and the queue's 3 baseline messages were still present, consumed all 3 successfully from node3 while node2 was down, and also published a new message during the outage — all succeeded. Restored node2 and confirmed full 3-node cluster health and message consumption. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id baselines and healthy cluster/queue state for all three nodes, then rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time, quorum preserved for the other two during each restart), polled each until reachable, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, confirmed RabbitMQ auto-started and rejoined the cluster (all three Disk Nodes and Running Nodes present, queue leader present, 3 Raft members intact), and verified publish/consume worked from each node post-restart. Password for app_user was passed via secret_env in all commands except one early rabbitmqctl add_user call where it was inadvertently passed literally; it was immediately rotated afterward via secret_env so no literal credential remains valid or exposed in the final report.
actions_performed: Installed rabbitmq-server (v4.2.7) + erlang27 via apk on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS mappings on all nodes
Generated a shared Erlang cookie and distributed it identically to /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie on all nodes with 0400 perms
Set NODENAME in /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-env.conf per node (rabbit@node1/2/3)
Started and enabled (rc-update) rabbitmq-server on all nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl stop_app/join_cluster/start_app, forming a 3-node cluster
Created `payments` vhost, created `app_user` (rotated password via secret_env), granted full permissions on payments vhost
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin; used it plus local guest admin (permissioned on payments) to declare a durable quorum queue `orders`
Installed python3 + py3-pika on all three nodes; wrote publish.py/consume.py test scripts using app_user credentials over AMQP
Published 3 durable baseline messages via node1
Stopped rabbitmq-server on node2 (simulated node loss), verified quorum (node1+node3) and the 3 messages remained in the queue, consumed all 3 from node3, published 1 more message during the outage
Restarted node2's rabbitmq-server, verified full 3-node cluster health, consumed the remaining message to empty the queue
Captured baseline boot_id and cluster health on node1, node2, node3

Sequentially rebooted node1 -> node2 -> node3 (one at a time), polling each until exec was available again, confirming changed boot_id, confirming rabbitmq-server auto-started and rejoined the cluster, and confirming publish/consume worked post-restart on each node
Confirmed quorum was preserved (2 of 3 nodes running RabbitMQ) during each individual node's reboot window

evidence.requirement: RabbitMQ installed and joined into a single cluster across node1, node2, node3
evidence.summary: All three nodes started RabbitMQ; node2 and node3 successfully joined node1's cluster; cluster_status from node1 shows all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes.

evidence.requirement: `payments` vhost created with an application account (app_user) able to publish/consume
evidence.summary: payments vhost and app_user created with full configure/write/read permissions scoped to payments; password subsequently rotated via secret_env.

evidence.requirement: Durable queue created, replicated across all nodes
evidence.summary: Quorum queue `orders` declared durable in payments vhost with members [rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3], online on all three.

evidence.requirement: Messages survive the loss of one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: 3 durable messages published via node1; node2's rabbitmq-server stopped; cluster_status confirmed quorum (node1+node3) preserved and queue still held 3 messages; all 3 messages consumed successfully from node3 while node2 was down; a 4th message published during the outage also succeeded; node2 restarted and rejoined; remaining message consumed, queue confirmed empty/healthy afterward.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/queue state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 06660b56... captured with healthy 3-node cluster; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id dec5be28... (changed) confirmed via exec repoll; rabbitmq-server auto-started, rejoined cluster (all 3 running); publish+consume succeeded through node1 post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/queue state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 53c8268a... captured with healthy 3-node cluster; reboot issued; quorum (node1+node3) confirmed preserved during outage; post-reboot boot_id 9fc91337... (changed) confirmed; rabbitmq-server auto-started, rejoined cluster; publish+consume succeeded through node2 post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/queue state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 043d4a24... captured with healthy 3-node cluster; reboot issued; quorum (node1+node2) confirmed preserved during outage; post-reboot boot_id 2278e1d7... (changed) confirmed; rabbitmq-server auto-started, rejoined cluster; publish+consume succeeded through node3 post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster and cross-node functional verification after all three restarts
evidence.summary: node2's cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running; node1 net_adm:ping to node3 returns pong; queue Raft members list all 3 nodes with online leader on node2; a message published from node1 was successfully consumed from node3, confirming end-to-end cross-node durability and consumability post-restart.
